pack.name: The Unquiet Marches — Book One Canon Pack

characters.name: Kael Vorn
characters.role: contract captain known as the Iron Captain
characters.status_end_book_one: alive; residing in the northern stone chamber
characters.public_truth: A highly effective captain whose reputation began at the Ridge Road and whose later work is morally disputed.
characters.private_book_one_truth: He experiences the Surge and the Hollow but believes them to be states of discipline, appetite and aftermath rather than magic.
boundaries: cannot be reduced to a quest giver
does not seek followers after Book One

characters.name: Sera
characters.role: practical authority and household keeper at the House of Wool
characters.status_end_book_one: alive; remains at the House of Wool
characters.public_truth: She controls operations through judgement, contracts, observation and clear boundaries.
boundaries: her choices do not exist only to develop Kael

characters.name: Mael Serrin
characters.status_end_book_one: alive; working for the Ashen Crossing merchants' council
characters.public_truth: He converts power into language, charters and enforceable procedure.
boundaries: culpable but not the sole cause of Reshen

characters.name: Edric Vale
characters.status_end_book_one: alive; exact current location not fixed
characters.public_truth: He records positions, names and omissions that official maps conceal.
drives: refusal to live quietly with falsified record

characters.name: Lord Caeden
characters.role: Marcher lord and sponsor of the Reshen road project
characters.status_end_book_one: alive as of the Ashen Crossing confrontation
characters.public_truth: A courteous and controlled lord who uses procedure and contractors to obtain strategic outcomes.
boundaries: cannot be killed by the GM in canon-adjacent mode

characters.name: Davan
characters.role: nineteen-year-old soldier at the crossroads garrison
characters.public_truth: Fair-haired, lean, still and watchful; drawn to the clean feeling of decisive violence.

characters.name: Mara Venn
characters.status_end_book_one: alive; travelled west from Ashen Crossing
characters.public_truth: An older physician with a damaged left eye who speaks plainly about responsibility and uncertainty.

characters.name: Joren
characters.role: Kael's lieutenant during the early campaigns
characters.public_truth: A capable subordinate whose obedience and field judgement show the consequences of command.

characters.name: Fen Arlen
characters.public_truth: Killed during the Reshen operation; his name and petition history become evidence of what official language removed.

characters.name: Oren Marr
characters.role: merchant owner of the House of Wool
characters.public_truth: Owns the house and commercial risks that Sera manages more competently in practice.

characters.name: Pellan
characters.public_truth: Careful, procedural and useful; often carries unwelcome facts to Sera.

characters.name: Renn
characters.role: corporal commanding the crossroads garrison in the captain's absence
characters.public_truth: Maintains authority with inadequate men and resources.

characters.name: Edran
characters.public_truth: Helps repair the stone chamber while preserving fair exchange and local independence.

characters.name: Ressa
characters.role: older resident of the northern valley
characters.public_truth: Carries local memory of the ruined fort and treats abandoned authority as practical material.

locations.name: Ridge Road
locations.summary: The rain-soaked site of the caravan attack where Kael's Iron Captain reputation begins.

locations.name: Reshen Valley
locations.type: three hamlets, mill, roads and farmland
locations.summary: A valley cleared under Caeden's commission. It is the central moral wound of Book One.

locations.name: Caeden's Seat
locations.summary: The court from which Caeden's road project and Reshen commission are authorised.

locations.name: House of Wool
locations.type: merchant household, warehouses and counting rooms
locations.summary: Oren Marr's wool house, managed in practice by Sera. A centre of trade, contracts, information and household authority.

locations.name: Lesten Market
locations.summary: Destination for the House of Wool convoy through the scrub route.

locations.name: Marrow Ford
locations.summary: A disputed crossing where legal claims, commercial urgency and armed pressure produce deaths.

locations.name: Ashen Crossing
locations.type: market village at three roads and a river
locations.summary: A trade settlement built around an old stone bridge and a newer timber span. Mael works for its merchants' council.

locations.name: Crossroads Garrison
locations.summary: A neglected garrison built for thirty and occupied by twelve, where Kael meets Davan.

locations.name: The Northern Stone Chamber
locations.type: ruined hill fort above a valley
locations.summary: An abandoned fort where Kael repairs one chamber and begins his written account.

locations.name: Caer Ashe
locations.summary: A significant trade and records centre referenced by characters and beneficiary ties.

locations.name: Marden
locations.summary: A site where road labour, debt and fortification reveal the architecture of local power.

factions.name: House Caeden
factions.public_goal: secure roads, grain movement and territorial authority
factions.game_pressure: offers lawful work whose full purpose is concealed

factions.name: House of Wool
factions.public_goal: move wool, cloth and contracts through dangerous roads
factions.game_pressure: commercial urgency collides with local rights and imperfect law

factions.name: District Garrisons
factions.public_goal: maintain roads and order with insufficient resources
factions.game_pressure: duty ends where jurisdiction, budget or personal risk becomes inconvenient

factions.name: Ashen Crossing Merchants' Council
factions.public_goal: consolidate bridge rights and guarantee winter passage
factions.game_pressure: efficient infrastructure can erase inherited livelihoods

factions.name: Broken Wheel Riders
factions.public_goal: uncertain; described through hostile reports and road activity
factions.game_pressure: official reports may exaggerate, misidentify or exploit their presence

factions.name: Harren Clans
factions.public_goal: protect clan territory and political autonomy
factions.game_pressure: Heartlands and Marcher propaganda often flatten them into a hostile category

factions.name: The Compact
factions.public_goal: provide common legal and political order
factions.game_pressure: local institutions invoke the Compact selectively

factions.name: Borrowed-War Lordships
factions.public_goal: defend bridges, levies, farms and prestige
factions.game_pressure: small disputes become war without a formal declaration

chapters.title: A Compiler of Fragments
chapters.summary: Aldric Vane frames the surviving account as evidence rather than acquittal and identifies Kael's error: mistaking urgency and narrowing for moral clarity.

chapters.title: The Stone Chamber
chapters.summary: An older Kael sits in a ruined northern fort during a storm and prepares to write the next true thing.

chapters.title: The Ridge
chapters.summary: Kael surveys a caravan attack in hard rain and chooses the civilian right flank.

chapters.title: The Riverbank
chapters.summary: Kael leads the descent, restores order in mud and smoke, and moves toward the raider captain.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Kael defeats the raider captain as the Surge intensifies and wonders how far the feeling can take him.

chapters.title: The Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: The dead and survivors are counted, the story hardens, and the title Iron Captain attaches to Kael.

chapters.title: A Cartographer’s Measure
chapters.summary: Edric maps the Ridge Road accurately and identifies the dangerous logic behind Caeden's Reshen interest.

chapters.title: Lord Caeden
chapters.summary: Caeden summons Kael and introduces the road-security purpose that will become the Reshen commission.

chapters.title: Permission
chapters.summary: Caeden and Mael define broad authority while omissions and operational language transfer responsibility toward Kael.

chapters.title: Three Hamlets
chapters.summary: Kael enters Reshen and turns its people, roads, stores and possible resistance into an operational field.

chapters.title: The Mill Road
chapters.summary: Resistance, smoke, fire and ambiguous categories collapse civilian life into hostile action.

chapters.title: The Second Evening
chapters.summary: The operation ends without tactical failure, but the Hollow no longer feels ordinary.

chapters.title: The Debt of Maps
chapters.summary: Edric presents the second map, omitted names and evidence that the official purpose concealed a road seizure.

chapters.title: Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Kael leaves and begins an autopsy of his own decisions without accepting easy absolution.

chapters.title: The House of Wool
chapters.summary: Sera hires Kael for a convoy and evaluates the man beneath the Iron Captain reputation.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Kael and Sera establish contractual, personal and consensual boundaries around authority and power.

chapters.title: The Iron Captain
chapters.summary: Kael's reputation becomes part of the House of Wool's defence while Sera tests whether destructive power can choose precision.

chapters.title: The River Crossing
chapters.summary: A commercial crossing dispute becomes armed conflict; Henric and Toman die inside a contract Kael accepted.

chapters.title: What Comes After
chapters.summary: Widows, beneficiaries and household records force the human cost into the room; Sera witnesses Kael's absence.

chapters.title: The Man at Her Table
chapters.summary: Kael answers the dead without recruiting them into purpose and leaves Sera rather than pretending transformation is complete.

chapters.title: The Names of Men
chapters.summary: Kael begins tracing Mael and converts names into coordinates, repeating the instrumental logic he condemns.

chapters.title: Borrowed Wars
chapters.summary: For eighteen months Kael follows Mael through minor wars, drawing moral lines without escaping the structures that employ him.

chapters.title: The Market Stall
chapters.summary: After temporarily abandoning the search, Kael sees Mael in Ashen Crossing and follows him into an alley.

chapters.title: Grey Rain
chapters.summary: Mael admits what he knew, identifies Kael's part in Reshen and refuses to become a simple enemy.

chapters.title: The Wall
chapters.summary: Kael holds Mael at sword point while the full chain of differentiated responsibility remains visible.

chapters.title: The Gap
chapters.summary: Kael spares Mael without extracting gratitude, obedience or proof that restraint will produce a good future.

chapters.title: The Crossroads Garrison
chapters.summary: Kael recognises the Surge's appeal in Davan and refuses the young soldier's request to follow.

chapters.title: A Question Answered
chapters.summary: Kael teaches Davan to notice what the clean feeling removes and sends him back with Orris Pell's name.

chapters.title: Northbound
chapters.summary: Kael travels without a target, finds an abandoned northern fort and considers staying.

chapters.title: The Stone Chamber
chapters.summary: Kael repairs one room, accepts village terms and begins preserving names without turning them into self-defence.

chapters.title: The First Winter
chapters.summary: Stillness exposes uncertainty; Kael records names, questions and the limits of his first interpretations.

chapters.title: The First Line
chapters.summary: During a storm, Kael writes the opening sentence of the account the reader has just read.

resolution.natural_1: creates a serious complication without forcing stupidity

hp.zero_rule: defeat state determined by established stakes

3: Storm Act within Book One manifestation limits

surge.overdraw: each missing Surge becomes one Hollow plus immediate complication

thresholds.4: bond, reputation or conviction under active strain

claims.text: The published Book One is The Noise of Purpose, Book One of The Unquiet Marches, by P A Myint.
The protagonist is Kael Vorn.
Kael becomes known as the Iron Captain after the Ridge Road battle.
At the Ridge Road, Kael chooses the civilian right flank while leaving the raider captain initially free.
Caeden commissions the Reshen operation through broad road-security and hostile-support language.
The Reshen operation causes civilian deaths, fire, seizure and dispossession despite no tactical failure.
Edric preserves a second account through maps, names and omissions.
Sera exercises practical authority over the House of Wool through judgement, contracts and household management.
Sera and Kael establish explicit terms and consensual boundaries around authority.
Henric and Toman die because the Marrow Ford contract becomes armed conflict.
Mael Serrin is alive at the end of the Ashen Crossing confrontation.
Mael works for the Ashen Crossing merchants' council on bridge-right consolidation.
Davan is alive and returns toward the crossroads garrison after speaking with Kael.
Kael ends Book One in the northern stone chamber and writes the first line of his account.
Rare supernatural phenomena are publicly believed to exist in the wider world.
Book One magic is rare, ambiguous and culturally interpreted rather than routine spellcasting.
Kael does not know that the Surge and Hollow may belong to the world's deeper power.
The default player character is original and does not replace a canonical protagonist.
The game is open-world and must accept free-form player intent.
Published Book One anchor events remain fixed in canon-adjacent mode.

rumours.claim: The Iron Captain killed forty raiders alone.
Reshen held a large organised rebel force.
The Harren Clans are a single barbarian horde.
Some soldiers become impossible to stop when thunder answers them.
The Orren tannery never held lawful bridge rights.
Edric Vale falsified maps to damage Caeden.

forbidden_public_assertions: Kael's Surge has a fully explained named cosmological source.
The player is the singular chosen saviour of the world.
Mael died in the Ashen Crossing alley.
The Reshen operation was a clean battle against a confirmed standing army.
Sera exists only as Kael's subordinate or reward.
Davan is already Kael's formal apprentice.
Routine resurrection, teleportation or public combat spell schools exist in the Book One Marches.
The former name Vaen is Kael's canonical name.
Stormwright is the current series identity.
